title: Throughput-stable continuous batcher with KV spill-tiering for mixed-length prompt/response workloads
creator: Aisha Verma
description: We observe throughput collapse and increased p99 latency in mixed prompt/response workloads where short prompts interleave with long completions. Current continuous-batcher admission policy overfills GPU KV residency causing frequent large-scale evictions and rehydrations. This ticket proposes a combined scheduler + KV spill-tiering approach to stabilize throughput and reduce costly full-page rehydrations.
background: Production traces (console dashboards) show patterns: bursts of short requests followed by long generation tasks cause KV working set spikes. When KV residency exceeds soft limits, the eviction policy aggressively frees pages, including hot pages, leading to rehydration thundering and p99 spikes. Prior attempts (soft-reserve, slot-tenure tweaks) reduced some churn but didn't eliminate cross-talk between short and long-turn cohorts.
problem_statement: How can we tune the continuous batching scheduler and KV residency management to keep steady tokens/sec and bounded p99 latency when serving mixed-length dialogues without regressing average throughput or increasing unit cost substantially?
proposal: Introduce a throughput-stable admission controller and a KV spill-tiering mechanism: 1) Admission controller: cohort-aware sliding horizon that measures per-cohort token density and enforces soft admission caps per cohort to avoid sudden working set spikes. 2) KV spill-tiering: implement a two-tier KV residency: - Tier A: GPU-resident hot pages (low-latency), maintained by residency score. - Tier B: compressed/quantized host-pinned memory (fast spill), with graded compression (FP16->INT8) and metadata to allow low-cost rehydration. Eviction prefers demoting to Tier B over discarding. 3) Background compaction: opportunistic compaction and proactive demotion during low-util windows. 4) Integration: scheduler exposes per-request expected completion length to admission controller and tags KV residency hints.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (experiment stub): add admission controller flags in scheduler, simulate Tier B via serialized KV buffers in host pinned region. Phase 2 (engineer): implement demotion path, compression codec, and residency scores. Phase 3 (validation): run synthetic workload sweep and a canary on dedicated GPU pool. Phase 4 (rollout): gradual rollout with traffic shadowing and monitoring alarms.
changes_summary: - Scheduler: new sliding-horizon cohort admission limiter, token-density estimator, and per-slot residency hint injection. - KV manager: two-tier residency API, demote/rehydrate paths, compression layer, background compactor. - Metrics: expose kv_residency_tierA_bytes, kv_demotion_rate, kv_rehydrate_latency_histogram, cohort_admit_reject_rate.
experiment_plan: Construct three synthetic mixes: A) baseline short-only, B) long-only, C) mixed 70% short prompts (10-50 tokens) and 30% long completions (800-2000 tokens). Run experiments on a 4xA100 canary pool with and without spill-tiering. Collect 6-hour runs, steady-state window analysis after warmup. Compare p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU memory pressure, and additional CPU/host-memory overhead.
success_criteria: p99 generation latency reduced by >=30% on mixed workload compared to current baseline
tokens/sec delta within +/-5% of baseline (no >5% throughput regression)
additional host memory overhead under 20% of GPU memory footprint
risk_mitigation: If demotion causes unacceptable rehydration CPU load, throttle demotion and increase compression ratio incrementally.
Provide opt-out flag per-customer for Dedicated/Private until validated.
Add conservative default thresholds and enable aggressive logging for the first 48h of rollout.
Run load-shedding policy that favors short-turn latency under extreme pressure to protect PLG UX.
rollout_plan: Feature branch -> internal integration tests -> perf bench run on synthetic traffic
Canary: enable on 1% of production traffic (non-enterprise tenants) during low-traffic hours
Expand to dedicated pools progressively (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with automated rollback if p99 increases or CPU host memory > threshold
Post-rollout: 2-week observation window with nightly summary reports
